role.altitude: The artist keeps composing, painting, choosing work and talking with clients and buyers; searching for reference photos, repainting colour studies, retyping catalogue details, laying out mailings and writing promotional texts from scratch shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping one catalogue of works that feeds site, portfolio and mailings
Editing drafted texts into their own voice
role.ambitious_version: An artist whose catalogue, portfolio and mailings run from one record, leaving the studio hours for the work.

tasks.short: Gather reference images, make composition and colour studies, and integrate and develop visual elements such as line, space, mass, color and perspective in the artwork.

steps.what: Artist gathers reference images and earlier studies for the piece
Artist makes thumbnail sketches and colour studies
Artist integrates and develops line, space, mass, color and perspective in the work to produce the desired effect

tasks.design: The artist's own reference photos and earlier studies are kept in a tagged image library, so finding material takes less time. Colour variations are tried on a scanned or photographed sketch in an image editor instead of repainting each study. No generated images enter the work. Developing the work stays fully with the artist.
tasks.previous_blocker: References sat in boxes and folders, and every colour study was painted again.
tasks.enabler_now: Tagged image libraries and image editors on a tablet.
tasks.still_hard: Media whose effect only shows in the physical material.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when the piece says what it should.
tasks.altitude: Little changes in making the work.

evidence.claim: A German court denied copyright protection to AI-generated logos despite a long prompt; generated images are kept out of the work.
Image editors let artists try colour variations on a photographed sketch.

assumptions: Boundary: developing the visual elements; studying techniques (task 10997) and shading and filling sketches (task 11003) are sibling tasks.
Developing the work keeps its full time.
unknowns: How much the artist works from reference.
research_questions: Does the artist try more colour options before committing?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: work from life with few studies; high: work from reference with many colour studies.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect the brief, confer with clients, editors, writers and art directors on the nature and content of the artwork, write, check and send the commission confirmation, and answer follow-up questions.

steps.what: Artist collects the brief: size, use, deadline and budget
Artist confers with clients, editors, writers or art directors on the nature and content of the artwork
Artist writes the commission confirmation: content, size, fee, deadline and rights
Artist sends the confirmation to the client
Artist answers follow-up questions from the client

approvals.approved_version: The confirmation text with content, size, fee, deadline and rights as checked by the artist in s4, addressed to the client; any change needs a new check before sending.

tasks.design: A commission request form on the artist's site asks for size, use, deadline and budget, so the first mails back and forth fall away. The conversation about content stays personal. The confirmation is filled in a template with standard clauses on fee, deadline and rights, including whether any tools were used that affect ownership. The artist checks it and sends that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefs arrived as loose mails and confirmations were written each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Site request forms and confirmation templates.
tasks.still_hard: Clients who do not know what they want.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what the client means behind what they say.

evidence.claim: A client may not own AI-generated work, so commission terms should say how tools are used.

assumptions: Boundary: agreeing the content of artwork; submitting work for approval (task 10992) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: about 60% of clients use the request form; s1 is priced at that share.
The conversation, checking, sending and follow-up keep their full time.

incremental.description: Artist keeps the confirmation template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few clients using the form; high: regular commissions with standard terms.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Photograph finished work, catalogue it, select work to maintain portfolios of artistic work, and update the portfolio site and printed portfolio.

steps.what: Artist edits the photos and catalogues each work with title, size, medium and year
Artist selects and orders work for the portfolio to show styles, interests and abilities
Artist updates the portfolio website and the printed or PDF portfolio

tasks.design: Each work gets one catalogue entry with photo, title, size, medium, year and status in a portfolio tool, instead of a spreadsheet plus separate folders. The portfolio site and the PDF portfolio are both built from the same entries, so a selection is made once and published to both. Photographing and selecting stay with the artist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site, PDF and spreadsheet were each updated by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Portfolio tools that publish a site and a PDF from one catalogue.
tasks.still_hard: Large or 3D work that is hard to photograph well.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing which works tell a coherent story.

reach.learn: Whether portfolios are current when asked for.

evidence.claim: Portfolio tools publish a website and a PDF from one catalogue of works.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping the portfolio; submitting work to shows (task 20994) is a sibling task.
Photographing and selecting keep their full time.
unknowns: How often the portfolio is updated.
research_questions: Is the portfolio more often up to date?

incremental.description: Artist moves older entries from the spreadsheet into the catalogue once.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few works per year; high: a large body of work updated often.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide what to promote, write texts, lay out brochures and mailings, check the final materials, send mailings and publish on web sites to market artwork, and answer buyers.

steps.what: Artist decides which work to promote, to whom and when
Artist writes texts for brochures, mailings and the website

loop.input: The catalogue entries for the chosen works, the exhibition details and the artist's own notes.
loop.output: Draft texts for the mailing, the brochure and the web page.
loop.check: Every title, size, price, date and venue must match the catalogue or the exhibition details; the artist rewrites the text in their own voice.
loop.stop: The artist keeps a text, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each exhibition and audience needs its own wording.

steps.what: Artist lays out brochures and mailings with images
Artist checks and approves the final materials
Artist sends the mailing to the subscriber list and publishes the web page
Artist answers responses from buyers and collectors

approvals.approved_version: The mailing, brochure and web page as approved by the artist in s4, sent to the subscriber list as it stands at sending; any edit needs a new approval before sending.

tasks.design: Deciding what to promote stays with the artist. A drafting step writes mailing, brochure and web texts from the catalogue entries and exhibition details, every title, price and date matching the catalogue, and the artist rewrites them in their own voice. Brochures and mailings use templates with fixed areas filled from the catalogue. The artist approves the final versions and sends that version from a mailing tool that keeps the subscriber list and unsubscribes, instead of sending from their own mailbox. Answering buyers stays personal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Texts and layouts were made from scratch for each show and mailings sent by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates filled from a spreadsheet or catalogue and mailing tools with list management.
tasks.still_hard: Finding new buyers beyond the existing list.
tasks.human_edge: Writing about the work in a way only the artist can.

ambition.what: Send a short update with each new work instead of only before shows.

tasks.altitude: Less writing and layout; choosing and talking stay.

reach.learn: Whether more frequent updates lead to more studio visits.

evidence.claim: A design tool locks template areas and fills variants from a spreadsheet.
Mailing lists need subscribers' consent and an unsubscribe option.

assumptions: Boundary: marketing artwork; keeping the portfolio (task 10993) and submitting to galleries (task 20994) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2 and s3: catalogue entries kept under task 10993.
Deciding, approving and answering buyers keep their full time.
research_questions: Do more frequent updates bring more sales?

incremental.description: Artist keeps templates and the subscriber list tidy.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few mailings with much rewriting; high: regular mailings from a current catalogue.
